walkthroughs.body_html: Earth holds ~1.386 billion km3 of water. Of this, 97.5% is saline ocean; only 2.5% is freshwater. Of the freshwater, 68.7% is locked in the cryosphere (ice caps, glaciers), 30.1% is groundwater, and just 0.3% is surface water (lakes, rivers, wetlands). Residence times vary: atmospheric water ~9 days, rivers ~2 weeks, deep oceans ~3,200 years, Antarctic ice ~20,000 years.

Carbon stores (in petagrams of carbon, PgC): marine sediments and rocks ~100,000,000 PgC, deep ocean ~37,000 PgC, soils ~1,500 PgC, atmosphere ~875 PgC (rising), terrestrial vegetation ~550 PgC. Anthropogenic emissions add ~10 PgC/yr, of which ~3 PgC is absorbed by oceans (acidifying them) and ~3 PgC by terrestrial sinks, leaving ~4 PgC accumulating in the atmosphere.

Water and carbon cycles are biogeochemically coupled. Photosynthesis links them: 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. Transpiration moves water from soils to atmosphere; the Amazon transpires ~20 billion tonnes of water daily, generating flying rivers. Carbon sequestration in forests requires water; drought reduces NPP (net primary productivity). Warming accelerates the cycle, intensifying floods, droughts and feedbacks like permafrost thaw releasing CH4 and CO2.

Which is the largest active carbon store?

Terrestrial vegetation
Deep ocean
Soils
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).

mcqs.q: How do humans affect the carbon cycle?
options: Humans only affect the carbon cycle by breathing out CO2.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
By burning fossil fuels (releasing stored geological carbon to the atmosphere) and deforestation (reducing the biosphere store and releasing carbon).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between physical and economic water scarcity?
options: Water scarcity only happens in dry countries.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.

Physical scarcity is insufficient water supply for demand (e.g. arid regions); economic scarcity is inability to access available water due to lack of infrastructure or investment, despite water being present.
